title: Single Number (XOR)
description: XOR every value: pairs cancel to 0 and the loner survives. O(n) time, O(1) space.

notes: XOR is commutative and associative — order does not matter; all pairs cancel.
a ^ a === 0 and a ^ 0 === a are the two identities that make this work.
No hash set needed — the bit pattern itself stores the running parity.

options: 0 is the identity for XOR (a ^ 0 === a)

questions.q: Space complexity of this XOR approach?
Why does the order of the array not matter?

exercises.prompt: Fill in the XOR single-number trick.

L3.prompt: Write `singleNumber(nums)` where every value appears twice except one — return the loner using XOR. O(n) time, O(1) space. Log `singleNumber([4, 1, 2, 1, 2])`.
hints: XOR with itself = 0; XOR with 0 = unchanged.
Fold the array with ^= starting from 0.
